description.narrative: As per the Terms of Reference (TOR) the scope of this partnership will focus on the implementation of activities in FDMNs focusing on support to resilient food systems in Cox’s Bazar, with the following objectives: For COMPONENT 1: HOMESTEAD GARDENING • Restoration of natural resource base and support climate-resilient local food production • Linking production and value chain, strengthening to food demand and consumption COMPONENT 2: MUSHROOM PRODUCTION: To empower project participants by providing them with the skills and resources needed to cultivate mushrooms and create a scalable and replicable model for mushroom farming that can be implemented within communities and individual homes. COMPONENT 4: SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT (UPCYCLING): Enhance waste management initiatives to reduce the environmental degradation in camps. Provide vulnerable FDMNs income opportunity and portable skills in engaging up-cycling process consumption.

COMPONENT 1: HOMESTEAD GARDENING Target participants : 12,000 FDMNs ( 90% female & 2% person with disabilities) COMPONENT 2: MUSHROOM PRODUCTION Target participants : 50 (80% female & 10% person with disabilities) COMPONENT 4: SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT (UPCYCLING) Target Beneficiary : 400 FDMNs ( 50% female & 10% person with disabilities)

Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, has become the epicentre of a prolonged humanitarian crisis, hosting over 900,000 Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMNs) alongside vulnerable host communities. This crisis has led to significant socio-economic and environmental challenges, including heightened pressures on local resources, increased vulnerability to natural disasters, and limited livelihood opportunities. Humanitarian organizations are providing crucial support; however, funding shortfalls have led to reductions in food assistance, leaving many refugees with as little as $8 a month for food (WFP, 2023). Addressing these issues requires a multifaceted approach that strengthens resilience, enhances food security, and builds sustainable livelihoods. The World Food Programme (WFP) has been actively engaged in mitigating these challenges through its Cox’s Bazar Resilience Programme, focusing on building community resilience through natural resource management, youth engagement, and market linkage promotion. This programme is critical in aligning humanitarian efforts with long-term development goals to support both Rohingya refugees and host communities. In line with WFP’s objectives, Cordaid’s proposal aims to contribute to green skills development within refugee camps through activities such as homestead gardening, aquaculture, mushroom cultivation, and solid waste management. These activities will not only supplement food security but also promote eco friendly practices that contribute to environmental restoration. The initiative will engage youth and other vulnerable groups in developing skills that align with sustainable practices, thereby building resilience against environmental and socio-economic shocks. The environmental degradation in Cox’s Bazar, exacerbated by the demands for firewood and agricultural space, has significantly impacted forest resources, increasing the risks of landslides and other disasters. Green skills development within camps offers a pathway to reduce environmental impact while fostering self-reliance among the refugee population. Moreover, with Cox’s Bazar designated as an 'ecologically critical area,' sustainable practices in food production and waste management are essential to safeguarding the region's natural resources. Cordaid’s extensive experience in resilience programming, coupled with a focus on sustainable livelihoods, can contribute significantly to achieving the goals. By integrating climate-smart agricultural techniques and waste reduction practices, Cordaid’s approach aligns with WFP’s commitment to enhancing food systems and building resilience against shocks. This project will support Cox’s Bazar’s most vulnerable communities, empowering them with green skills that promote self-reliance and sustainability in the face of ongoing challenges. On that note, in alignment with the organization's track record and expertise, Cordaid in Bangladesh would like to offer support to WFP Bangladesh in addressing challenges around green skills, capacity strengthening and building the resilience of the local community, market linkage and anticipatory action activities. Project Justification The Cox’s Bazar region faces severe challenges in terms of food security, environmental degradation, and waste management due to the prolonged presence of a large refugee population. Activity 2 of the WFP Resilience Programme aims to address these challenges by promoting green skills development in the refugee camps, focusing on homestead gardening, mushroom cultivation, aquaculture, and solid waste management. Cordaid’s proposed interventions align with WFP’s objectives to foster sustainable food systems, enhance climate resilience, and create livelihood opportunities for vulnerable populations. Homestead gardening plays a critical role in improving food security and nutrition, particularly in crisis settings. Studies have shown that households engaged in homestead gardening experience better dietary diversity, with fresh vegetables contributing significantly to daily caloric and protein intake (Landon-Lane, 2011). In Cox’s Bazar, Cordaid’s plan to support 20,000 households in homestead gardening will enable refugees to grow nutrient-rich crops that supplement their food intake, directly supporting WFP’s goal of enhancing food security among populations affected by crises (WFP, 2025). In addition, aquaculture and mushroom cultivation offer sustainable avenues for increasing food availability and generating income. Aquaculture, which has been linked to a 20% improvement in protein intake in similar refugee settings, will be implemented to provide fresh fish for up to 1,000 households (FAO, 2020). Meanwhile, mushroom farming is a low-cost, high-nutrition activity well-suited to the resource constraints of refugee camps. By training households in mushroom cultivation, Cordaid aims to empower 200 households with skills that not only improve nutritional intake but also offer new income streams (UNDP, 2019). Addressing the urgent need for waste management, Cordaid’s upcycling program will transform plastic and aluminium waste into reusable products like gardening bags, directly integrating waste reduction with food production. This aligns with WFP’s objectives of promoting climate resilience and sustainable resource use. Research conducted by UNEP indicates that upcycling programs can reduce waste by 30% and increase household income by 15% (UNEP, 2021) which is relevant to this local context. Our proposed interventions align well with the WFP’s Strategic Objectives of enhancing food systems, building climate resilience, and supporting vulnerable communities in Cox’s Bazar. By developing green skills and fostering environmental stewardship, this project not only addresses immediate food security needs but also contributes to long-term resilience and self-reliance among refugees and host communities in Cox’s Bazar.
